system.name: CASSINI
system.one_liner: a network-aware job scheduler for ML clusters that computes time-shifts for jobs sharing network links

components.name: Themis arbiter
components.role: computes finish-time fairness, selects winning bids and proposes N placement candidates

components.name: Cassini module (Algorithm 2)
components.role: selects the best placement candidate and computes unique time-shifts for jobs sharing the network

components.name: Construct Affinity graphs
components.role: builds an affinity graph Gc for each placement candidate

components.name: Solve optimization formulation (Table 1)
components.role: solves the optimization to obtain compatibility scores for links in Gc

components.name: Select top placement candidate
components.role: picks the top placement candidate based on its compatibility metric

components.name: Compute unique time-shifts (Algorithm 1)
components.role: computes time-shifts for jobs that share the network under the chosen placement

components.name: Themis Agent
components.role: applies the received time-shifts at the start of the epoch on each server

flows.what: Final job placement and time-shifts ({t_j}, top_placement)

content.key_idea: CASSINI slots in between Themis's arbiter and its per-server agents: it takes the arbiter's multiple placement candidates, builds affinity graphs and solves an optimization to score link compatibility, then computes network-aware time-shifts that the existing Themis agents apply, closing the loop with performance metrics fed back to the arbiter.
content.reading_order: top-down: Themis arbiter proposes placement candidates, the Cassini module processes them through affinity-graph construction, optimization and candidate selection to compute time-shifts, then the GPU cluster's Themis agents apply them, with performance metrics looping back to the top.

summary: CASSINI is a network-aware job scheduler that augments existing ML schedulers like Themis rather than replacing them. Figure 9 shows this augmentation as a three-layer, top-down architecture. At the top, a peach-colored 'Themis arbiter' box computes finish-time fairness, selects winning bids and now proposes N placement candidates instead of one. These flow into a green 'Cassini module (Algorithm 2)' box in the middle, which constructs affinity graphs for each candidate, solves an optimization (Table 1) to score link compatibility, selects the top placement, and computes unique time-shifts (Algorithm 1) for jobs sharing network links. The result, final job placements and time-shifts, flows down into a yellow 'GPU Cluster' box where per-server Themis Agents apply them; performance metrics are fed back up to the arbiter via a dashed line on the left. The color-coded, layered layout makes clear which parts are CASSINI's contribution versus Themis's original components.
